element: Amougou Mbida & Angermeir (An Agentic Approach Towards Replication Package Quality Evaluation, ESEM 2026, arXiv:2606.02006v2)

UC1.note: Output is a markdown quality report against criteria (Sec 3 Phase 5), not a venue-format artifact appendix.

UC2.note: Discussion says the knowledge base 'can dynamically adapt to venue-specific checklists' (Sec 5, p.10) but the tool evaluates against a standard, never translates a package between standards.

UC3.evidence: Evaluation demands evidence-based reasoning with explicit citations (e.g., file paths, code snippets), defaulting to a fail status if required evidence is missing. (Sec 3, Phase 4, p.5)
UC3.note: File-path citations link criteria (not paper claims/results) to artifact components; 0 is defensible, though one could argue partial since it does produce criterion-to-file evidence links.

UC4.evidence: we implement a multi-agent prototype that inspects replication packages and produces evidence-grounded improvement reports. (Abstract, p.1); 'diagnoses specific shortcomings and generates a to-do list for artifact improvement' (Sec 5, p.10)

UC5.evidence: Because some requirements demand paper-text analysis rather than artifact inspection, we distinguish between the full set and a subset of 31 operationalized criteria that are fully amenable to automated, artifact-based evaluation. (Sec 4 RQ1, p.6)
UC5.note: The paper PDF is ingested only to extract metadata, locate the artifact, and provide RAG context; paper-text criteria are explicitly excluded from automated evaluation.

UC6.note: Suggests improvements but generates no code, environment, or docs.

UC7.note: Comparison is against consolidated guideline criteria, never against exemplar (P,A) pairs.

B1.evidence: We hope that our contribution in the long-term can support authors in improving their research artifact quality even before artifact review and to consequently reduce review overhead in artifact review tracks. (Sec 1, p.2)
B1.note: Framed as an author-side 'replication package linter' and piloted with authors on their own artifacts, but conclusion also targets AECs as a 'force multiplier'; 2-3 both defensible.

B2.evidence: evaluate each subtopic concurrently within isolated reasoning contexts over a shared, read-only filesystem, gathering evidence via pattern search and hybrid retrieval (lexical and semantic). (Sec 3, Phase 4, p.5)
B2.note: Never executes code; it does statically read source files (not only docs), so 2 would also be defensible, but 1 is fine given zero execution.

B3.evidence: The input paper is converted from PDF to markdown to extract key metadata (title, abstract, artifact details) and a global summary... A sub-agent extracts artifact references (e.g., GitHub, Zenodo, OSF) from the paper summary. (Sec 3, Phases 1-2, p.4)
B3.note: Pipeline entry point is the paper PDF (used to find the artifact and as RAG context), but all 31 operationalized criteria are judged on the artifact; 5 overstates artifact-only input.

B4.evidence: We consolidate 380 requirements from 34 sources into 51 reproducibility criteria, of which 31 are operationalized for automated artifact-based evaluation. (Abstract, p.1)
B4.note: Driven by an explicit, traceable criteria knowledge base derived from published venue/publisher guidelines (a consolidated meta-standard rather than one venue's).

B5.evidence: The structured output is transformed into a hierarchical markdown report aggregating evaluation metadata, paper summaries, and detailed criterion assessments linked to their guidelines. (Sec 3, Phase 5, p.5)
B5.note: Emits both per-criterion Pass/Fail/NA classifications (scored against baseline) and a prose improvement report/to-do list; 3 is right, 4 arguable given 'Rather than offering a simple pass-or-fail judgment' (Sec 5).

disagreements: B3: current 5, should be 4 because the pipeline starts from the paper PDF (Phase 1 ingests/summarizes/embeds the paper, Phase 2 extracts artifact links from it) even though the criteria are evaluated on the artifact.
one_line_summary: LangGraph multi-agent 'replication package linter' that ingests the paper, fetches the artifact, statically checks it against 31 guideline-derived criteria with HITL planning, and emits a markdown Pass/Fail plus improvement report.
